title: Learn Essential First Aid and CPR skills
content: Whether you're starting a new job, preparing for a volunteer role, completing a school placement or simply want to be ready when an emergency happens, the City of Kitchener offers First Aid & CPR Training to help residents build confidence and lifesaving skills.

The City offers WSIB-approved First Aid, CPR-C and AED training that is recognized by employers across Ontario. Participants receive certification valid for three years and gain practical, hands-on experience responding to workplace, home and community emergencies.
Courses are available on weekdays and weekends, making it easy to fit training into your schedule. Training options include:
Whether you're learning lifesaving skills for the first time or renewing your certification, there's a course to meet your needs.
These courses are ideal for employees, job seekers, post-secondary students, volunteers, caregivers, and anyone who wants to be prepared to help when it matters most.
Ready to get certified? Register online, at your local community centre, pool or the Service Kitchener counter at City Hall and take the first step toward becoming emergency ready.
Learn more and register:  First Aid & CPR Training

title: Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park to feature Canada's first multi-sport glass floor
content: Innovative technology will expand recreation opportunities, improve accessibility, and attract tournaments and events to Kitchener

Kitchener, ON – Residents visiting the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park will soon have access to a recreation experience unlike any other in Canada. Available for use starting in early 2027, the Centre’s new quad gymnasium will feature Canada's first multi-sport glass floor, making it home to one of the largest installations of its kind in the world.

The innovative multi-sport surface w ill provide more opportunities for recreation, sport, tournaments and community events while giving residents access to the same playing surface used for decades at sport venues and international competitions globally.

"Great community spaces should evolve alongside the people who use them," said Mayor Berry Vrbanovic. "The multi-sport glass floor reflects the kind of future we're building in Kitchener, one that embraces innovation while creating more diverse opportunities for residents to compete, connect and belong close to home. This floor gives the community access to a unique recreation experience typically found at premier sport venues and, as the first installation of its kind in Canada, will help create better recreational and competitive sport experiences while also attracting new events and visitors that support local businesses and strengthen Kitchener's economy."
The multi-sport glass floor will support a wide variety of sports including pickleball, basketball, volleyball, floor hockey, futsal, badminton, wheelchair basketball and wheelchair pickleball.

Starting November 14, when the Cowan Recreation Centre officially opens, visitors will have a unique opportunity to get a behind-the-scenes look at the technology that will be located beneath the multi-sport glass panels. Installation of the floor is expected to be complete early in the new year.

While this flooring system, designed and installed by ASB GlassFloor, is the first of its kind in C anada, it is used in the United States and across Europe, including venues in Germany, Greece, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

The flooring system uses LED lighting located under glass floor panels to display digital sport lines directly onto the playing surface. Unlike traditional gymnasium floors that rely on multiple p ermanently painted or taped lines, the sport lines on this floor can be quickly and easily reconfigured at the touch of a button depending on which sport is being played. Only the lines required for the sport being played are displayed at any time, reducing visual clutter and creating a cleaner environment that can be easier for participants to navigate. Importantly, flexible sport configurations also mean more support for accessible and inclusive play – transitioning from wheelchair basketball to wheelchair pickleball and back to traditional volleyball is easy and safe.

With a surface that exceeds internationally recognized standards for shock absorption and slip resistance, combined with a durable, high-performance surface that supports wheelchair sports and adaptive recreation programming, the technology helps create a more inclusive recreation experience for residents of all abilities. The floor is certified by the International Basketball Federation (FIBA), International Volleyball Federation (FIVB), and International Handball Federation (IHF).

Beyond enhancing the user experience, the floor was selected for its long-term value. The multi-sport glass floor does not require refinishing or resurfacing on a regular basis and can accommodate a broader range of activities without protective floor coverings. Less downtime and fewer seasonal maintenance closers mean lower maintenance costs and more programming time for residents.

By combining digital flexibility, enhanced accessibility and reduced maintenance requirements, the glass sports floor creates new possibilities for how the space can be programmed and used while delivering long-term value for residents and the community.
Quick facts
First glass sports floor installation in Canada
One of the largest installations in the world
Can be reconfigured at the touch of a button to support a wide range of sports
Only the lines required for the activity being played are displayed
Supports wheelchair sports and adaptive recreation programming
No sanding, resurfacing or seasonal shutdowns required
About the Cowan Recreation Centre at RBJ Schlegel Park
The Cowan Recreation Centre is among the largest and most sustainable municipally owned recreation centres in Canada.

The Centre offers diverse recreation opportunities with a quad gymnasium, FIFA-sized indoor turf field, cricket practice nets, competition and leisure pools, and an indoor walking track, supporting sports and activities ranging from basketball and soccer to pickleball, badminton and swimming.

The facility is the most accessible building ever constructed by the City of Kitchener, designed to meet the City's highest accessibility standards and shaped through input from residents with lived experience. It features pool ramps, wider pathways, tactile wayfinding elements and accessible viewing areas.
Built to host provincial and national competitions, tournaments and major events, the Centre will help showcase Kitchener, support local businesses and generate economic benefits for the community.

title: Statement from Mayor Vrbanovic on Ontario’s 2026 Economic Outlook and Fiscal Review
content: Today’s provincial economic update comes at a time when many Kitchener businesses and workers are dealing with real uncertainty caused by U.S. tariffs and changing global trade conditions.

Ontario’s 2026 Economic Outlook and Fiscal Review includes measures aimed at supporting workers and businesses, including the recently announced $8.7-billion Canada-Ontario action plan for tariff-affected sectors, expanded access to provincial trade and financing programs, and employment and training supports for workers affected by layoffs.

Here in the City of Kitchener, we know that ours is one of Canada’s most trade-exposed regions, and 15 per cent of our workforce is employed in manufacturing. Behind those numbers are local families, small businesses, manufacturers and employers who contribute every day to the strength of our community.

That’s why we welcome the province’s continued focus on helping workers and businesses respond to tariff pressures. These supports can help local employers manage uncertainty, pursue new opportunities and, most importantly, keep people working.

We’re doing our part as well. Through our Tariff and Trade Task Force and Plan to Support Local and Protect Jobs , we’re bringing local partners together, using City spending to support Canadian and local businesses, and helping Kitchener companies adapt and reach new markets. Measures that reduce the cost of investment and research can also help our manufacturing and innovation sectors continue to invest and create jobs here at home.

Municipalities have an essential role in Ontario’s economic future. The roads, transit, water systems and other infrastructure we build and maintain help create jobs and make new housing and private investment possible. As Kitchener continues to grow, we need strong, predictable and long-term provincial investment in municipal infrastructure so we can keep pace with that growth.

We’re also pleased to see continued progress on the new Highway 7 between Kitchener and Guelph, including the replacement of the Frederick Street bridge, as well as recent improvements along the Kitchener GO Line. Better connections give people more options to get to work and help connect Kitchener businesses to opportunities across Ontario.

We’ll continue working with the Province of Ontario and our partners to make sure Kitchener workers and businesses can access the supports they need, while continuing to advocate for the infrastructure a growing Kitchener and Waterloo Region need for the future.

title: Kitchener Fire Department: Major incident report – October 27, 2026
content: At 5:30 a.m. this morning, Kitchener Fire crews responded to reports of a residential structure fire on Weber St E.
All occupants safely self-evacuated. Fire spread was contained to contents only.  Residents of the main floor apartment will be displaced and are being supported.
There are no reported civilian or firefighter injuries at this time.
The cause of the fire remains under investigation. Kitchener Fire is working closely with Waterloo Regional Police Service.

title: Make your mark: Vote today in the 2026 municipal and school board election
content: Kitchener, ON - Today, residents across Ontario, including Kitchener, will shape their community’s future by voting in the 2026 municipal and school board election.
From local roads, parks and community programs to regional services and school board representation, the decisions made by elected officials have an impact on everyday life.
Before you head to your voting location:
Confirm you're eligible to vote
You must be a Canadian citizen, at least 18 years old, and live in Kitchener, own or rent property in Kitchener, or be the spouse of an owner or tenant.
Know when and where to vote
Cast your ballot between 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. on October 26.
Before you leave home, find your voting location. You can vote anywhere in your ward on Election Day.
Bring identification
If you're not on the voters list, you can still vote if you're eligible. Bring identification showing your name and current address.
Make an informed choice
Review the candidates running in your ward and school board positions before casting your ballot.
Whether this is your first municipal election or you've voted for years, every ballot helps shape the future of our community.
Visit KitchenerVotes.ca for voting locations, voter information and election results.
Make your mark. Local matters.

title: Tips for using fireworks safely and responsibly this Diwali
content: As residents prepare to celebrate Diwali, the Festival of Lights, the City of Kitchener is reminding everyone to prioritize safety and exercise caution when using fireworks during the holiday.
For those planning private fireworks displays, the City encourages residents to familiarize themselves with the Fireworks and Firecrackers Bylaw , which was updated in 2025.
To keep everyone safe and in compliance with City bylaws, please follow these rules when setting off fireworks:
You must be 18 years or older to set off fireworks.
Fireworks can only be set off on private property.
Fireworks are only permitted during approved dates and times.
Fireworks must be set off at least 10 meters away from any building or structure.
Failure to follow these rules may result in enforcement action or fines.
Setting off fireworks in public spaces, including parks, roadways, schoolyards and other public property, is not permitted.
Residents choosing to use fireworks are encouraged to take the following precautions:
Follow all manufacturer instructions and safety guidelines.
Use fireworks only in permitted locations and maintain a safe distance from buildings, structures and spectators.
Keep water nearby in case of an emergency.
Never attempt to relight fireworks that have malfunctioned.
Be considerate of neighbours, pets and others who may be affected by loud noises.
The City continues to take a zero-tolerance approach to fireworks bylaw violations and works closely with Waterloo Regional Police to help protect public safety.
Setting off fireworks outside permitted areas or times could result in a minimum fine of  $1,500.
For fireworks related complaints, contact the Waterloo Regional Police Service at 519-585-8088 .
In the event of an emergency or dangerous situation, always call 911.
For more information about fireworks regulations, permitted locations and safety tips, visit Kitchener.ca/Fireworks .
The City of Kitchener wishes everyone celebrates a safe and happy Diwali.

title: Advance voting up 47 per cent in Kitchener's 2026 municipal and school board election
content: Kitchener, ON – Thousands of Kitchener residents have already cast their ballots in the 2026 municipal and school board election, with advance voting drawing strong participation across the city.

A total of 8,208 residents voted during advance voting opportunities held between October 8 to 20, representing four per cent of all eligible voters, and exceeding advance turnout in the 2022 election by 47 per cent.

"Our goal is to make voting as accessible and convenient as possible," said Amanda Fusco, Director of Legislative Services and City Clerk. "The community’s positive response to advance polling tells us residents care about local government and they value the flexible voting options we’ve provided this election."

This year's strong advance voting turnout highlights the impact of expanded voting opportunities designed to make participation easier and more accessible. For the first time, residents could take advantage of drive-thru voting, cast a ballot at any advance voting location across the city, and vote at convenient retail and community destinations through the City's "Shop and Vote" program. Combined with the addition of a fifth advance voting day, these flexible options helped remove barriers and provided more opportunities for residents to participate in the democratic process before Election Day.

While advance voting numbers provide an early indication of participation, residents who have not yet voted are encouraged to make a plan to cast their ballot on Election Day, Monday, October 26, 2026.
You must be a Canadian citizen, at least 18 years old, and live in Kitchener, own or rent property in Kitchener, or be the spouse of an owner or tenant.
Cast your ballot between 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. on October 26.
Before you leave home, find your voting location. You can vote anywhere in your ward on Election Day.
If you're not on the voters list, you can still vote if you're eligible. Bring identification showing your name and current address.
Review the candidates running in your ward and school board positions before casting your ballot.
Whether this is your first municipal election or you've voted for years, every ballot helps shape the future of our community.
Visit KitchenerVotes.ca for voting locations, voter information and election results.

title: Kitchener celebrates Small Business Week with free events for business owners
content: The City of Kitchener is celebrating Small Business Week with free workshops and networking events for aspiring entrepreneurs and small business owners. Interested residents are invited to register online through the Waterloo Region Small Business Centre .

From family-run shops to innovative startups, small businesses help shape the character and vitality of our city. This week is an opportunity to celebrate the entrepreneurs who make Kitchener unique and to encourage residents to support local businesses that contribute so much to our community every day by creating jobs, strengthening our community, and making Kitchener’s economy more competitive.
Small Business Exchange – Open Mic edition
October 23, 2026

More than traditional networking, this event brings together entrepreneurs and small business owners to exchange ideas, build partnerships, discover local services, and promote their businesses through networking, exhibitor displays, and an open mic business showcase. Register in advance .
Business Plan 101 (virtual)
October 27, 2026
Learn why a business plan is important for your business success and the steps to complete your own. Register in advance .
Newcomers Building Businesses in Waterloo Region
October 27, 2026

Kitchener has engaged with the Kitchener Public Library for a series called: New Ways to Work. This session will explore the experiences of women entrepreneurs who are building businesses, creating solutions and contributing to the local economy. Hear real stories about supports that made a difference. Register in advance.

The Waterloo Region Small Business Centre is part of the Ontario Small Business Advisory Centres (OSBACs) network, making it easier for entrepreneurs in our community to identify and access one-on-one consultations, training, provincial programs and grants at more than 50 locations across Ontario.
For more information, visit the Waterloo Region Small Business Centre website.
About Support Local. Build Kitchener.

Kitchener has always been a community of makers, builders, innovators and entrepreneurs. Every time we choose to support local, we contribute to the success of the businesses and people who help shape our city.

Every purchase helps build local businesses, create local jobs and build a more resilient Kitchener. When you choose to shop, dine, or do business locally, you're doing more than making a purchase. You're helping build a stronger Kitchener.
Learn more at Kitchener.ca/Support-Local .
About WRSBC

The Waterloo Region Small Business Centre is part of the Ontario Small Business Advisory Centres (OSBAC) network, which delivers provincially funded programs and services to help entrepreneurs and small businesses start, grow, and succeed. With more than 50 centres across Ontario, the OSBAC network supports local business growth and strengthens communities throughout the province.

Whether you have an idea, are looking to start your own business or want to grow your existing business , WRSBC advisors provide one-on-one consultations, inspiring people to start and grow sustainable businesses, here in Waterloo Region.
Learn more at WaterlooRegionSmallBusiness.com .
